spatial_claims.claim: Line a is bisected into halves h, so a = 2h; line d is formed by extending a by one more h, so d = 3h, giving a:d = 2:3
Mean proportional b is constructed between a and d; mean proportional c between a and b

configuration_map: All objects are line segments with algebraic length relationships: a = 2h, d = 3h (a extended by h along the same line), b = mean proportional of a and d, c = mean proportional of a and b. The configuration is purely one-dimensional with no angles, triangles, circles, or complex spatial relationships. The proof reasons entirely about ratios and commensurability of these segments.
skip_reason: The proof is purely algebraic/proportional. It establishes a numerical ratio (2:3), constructs line segments with that ratio via a trivial linear construction, then reasons entirely about commensurability and incommensurability using ratio arithmetic and number-theoretic propositions (8.8, 8.11, 10.6-10.9). There are no geometric configuration claims (no angles, no triangles, no circles, no inside/outside relationships) that could be contradictory. Book 10 is mixed and this proposition falls squarely on the algebraic side.
